help_text:
Usage: kasumi [--lang <code>] [command] [arguments] [options]

Daily commands:
  kasumi                       Show daemon and profile overview
  kasumi status [profile]      Show overview or pending local changes
  kasumi show <profile>        Show profile summary (--full for commit & history)
  kasumi logs [profile] [-f]   Show daemon logs (-f to follow live)
  kasumi start [--autostart]   Start the continuous background daemon
  kasumi stop                  Stop the background daemon
  kasumi pause <profile|--all> Pause automated sync ('resume' to unpause)
  kasumi sync <profile>        Synchronize immediately with remote storage
  kasumi conflicts <profile>   List or resolve local conflict files
  kasumi config                Interactive profile and daemon wizard

General options:
  -h, --help                   Show this help (--help --all for all commands)
  -v, --version                Show Kasumi version
  --lang <code>                Select language before the command (en, pt-BR)
  --full, --quiet, --json      Expand details, silence output, or emit JSON

Run 'kasumi --help --all' to list advanced and maintenance commands.
help_text_all:
Usage: kasumi [--lang <code>] <command> [subcommand] [arguments] [options]

Daily commands:
  kasumi                                       Show daemon and profile overview.
  kasumi status [<profile>] [--full]           Show overview or pending local changes.
  kasumi show <profile> [--full]               Show profile summary, local traceability, and daemon status.
  kasumi logs [<profile>] [-f] [--lines <n>]   Show daemon logs (-f to follow live; --full includes no-op polls).
  kasumi start [--autostart]                   Start background daemon (optionally enable user-session autostart).
  kasumi stop                                  Stop the running daemon gracefully.
  kasumi pause <profile|--all>                 Pause automated daemon sync/GC for a profile or all profiles.
  kasumi resume <profile|--all>                Resume automated daemon sync/GC for a profile or all profiles.
  kasumi sync <profile> [--full]               Synchronize with remote storage.
  kasumi conflicts <profile>                   List preserved local conflict artifacts.
  kasumi conflicts resolve <profile> <path>    Resolve a preserved conflict group (--keep-canonical | --keep).
  kasumi config                                Interactive profile and daemon wizard.

Advanced & profile management:
  kasumi list [--full]                         List profile names (or detailed table with --full).
  kasumi diagnostics [<profile>]               Inspect local environment, rclone toolchain, and profile health.
  kasumi key <profile> [--replace]             Re-enter and save the profile key.
  kasumi profile <subcommand> ...              Non-interactive profile management (create/edit/clone/storage/rename/delete/test).
  kasumi daemon <subcommand> ...               Full daemon subcommands (run/stop/status/sync/pause/resume/unlock/lock/reload/logs/autostart).
  kasumi ignore <subcommand> ...               Inspect or initialize .kasumiignore rules (check/init).
  kasumi sync <profile> --dry-run              Simulate without altering data.
  kasumi sync <profile> --initial              Initialize a missing local database (bootstrap or enroll).
  kasumi sync <profile> --audit-inventory      Sync, then structurally audit remote inventory.
  kasumi sync <profile> --repair               List remote inventory and re-upload missing objects from disk.
  kasumi fsck <profile>                        Audit remote integrity.
  kasumi gc <profile> [--dry-run] [--min-age <hours>]
                                               Analyze or run garbage collection on safe objects.
  kasumi gc remove-writer <profile> <writer-id>
                                               Remove one exact writer marker; verify its process is inactive.
  kasumi gc remove-barrier <profile> [--confirm-abandoned]
                                               Remove an abandoned maintenance barrier after manual verification.
  kasumi repack <profile> [--dry-run] [--reclaim-dirty] [--full]
                                               Consolidate fragmented Micro-Packs and loose small files.
  kasumi resolve-missing <profile> [--dry-run | --confirm]
                                               Resolve unavailable content as deleted.
  kasumi completion <bash|zsh|fish|powershell> Output shell completion script.

Remote inspection (read-only):
  kasumi remote heads <profile>                Current logical heads.
  kasumi remote tree <profile> [--head <id>]   Tree of a specific head.
  kasumi remote commits <profile>              Reachable commits.
  kasumi remote summary <profile> [--full]     General vault and activity summary.
  kasumi remote stat <profile> <path> [--commit <id>]          Properties of a path (or commit).
  kasumi remote log <profile> <path> [--full]                  Reachable commit history for a path.
  kasumi remote commit <profile> <id>                          Commit details.
  kasumi remote get <profile> <path> <dst> [--commit <id>]     Download authenticated file.
  kasumi remote restore <profile> [<prefix>] <dst>             Restore full snapshot or subtree into empty folder.
  kasumi remote epochs <profile>               Epoch chain.
  kasumi remote epoch <profile> <id>           Epoch details.
  kasumi remote contents <profile>             Contents by metadata.
  kasumi remote contents <profile> --audit     Cryptographic audit.
  kasumi remote content <profile> <id>         Content details.
  kasumi remote markers <profile>              Classify physical markers.
  kasumi remote objects <profile>              Physical namespace.
  kasumi remote orphans <profile>              List orphans; does not run GC.
  kasumi remote writers <profile>              Writers and barrier.
  kasumi remote health <profile>               Full remote health diagnostic.

General options:
  -h, --help                                   Show help message (--help --all for full list).
  -v, --version                                Show Kasumi version.
  --lang <code>                                Select language before the command.
  --quiet                                      Suppress progress, duration, and non-error operational output.
  --json                                       Emit machine-readable JSON output on supported commands.
  --log-file <path>                            Append clean execution logs (or NDJSON lines with --json) to <path>.
  --bwlimit <rate>, --concurrency <1..16>      Per-invocation transport bandwidth limit and transfer concurrency.

Use kasumi <command> [subcommand] --help for command-specific help.

command_help.sync:
Usage: kasumi sync <profile> [--dry-run | --initial | --audit-inventory | --repair] [--allow-empty-local] [--bwlimit <rate>] [--concurrency <1..16>] [--full]

Synchronize with remote storage. --dry-run simulates without altering data.
--initial initializes a missing local database.
--allow-empty-local permits syncing when an already populated profile has a missing or empty local folder.
--audit-inventory runs Sync then a structural audit; it cannot be combined with --dry-run or --initial.
--repair lists remote objects and re-uploads missing physical objects from verified local files; it cannot be combined with --dry-run or --initial.
--bwlimit <rate> and --concurrency <1..16> override profile transport settings for this run.
--full displays full stage statistics, transfer summaries, and all plan or pending items.
Example: kasumi sync Programming --dry-run
command_help.status:
Usage: kasumi status [<profile>] [--bwlimit <rate>] [--concurrency <1..16>] [--full]

With no profile, shows the consolidated daemon and profiles overview.
With <profile>, shows pending local changes. --full expands technical details.
Example: kasumi status
command_help.logs:
Usage: kasumi logs [<profile>] [-f | --follow] [--lines <1..1000>] [--full]

Show recent daemon activity (hides repetitive no-op polls by default; pass --full to show everything).
-f / --follow streams live events across Windows and Linux until Ctrl+C.
Example: kasumi logs Obsidian -f
command_help.start:
Usage: kasumi start [--autostart] [--json] [--quiet]

Start the continuous background sync daemon. Pass --autostart to also install login autostart.
Example: kasumi start --autostart
command_help.stop:
Usage: kasumi stop [--json] [--quiet]

Stop the running background daemon gracefully.
Example: kasumi stop
command_help.pause:
Usage: kasumi pause (<profile> | --all) [--json] [--quiet]

Pause automated daemon sync/GC for one profile or all profiles.
Example: kasumi pause --all
command_help.resume:
Usage: kasumi resume (<profile> | --all) [--json] [--quiet]

Resume automated daemon sync/GC for one profile or all profiles.
Example: kasumi resume --all
command_help.fsck:
Usage: kasumi fsck <profile> [--bwlimit <rate>] [--concurrency <1..16>]

Audit remote integrity and authenticated content.
Example: kasumi fsck Programming
command_help.gc:
Usage: kasumi gc <profile> [--dry-run] [--min-age <hours>] [--bwlimit <rate>] [--concurrency <1..16>]

Analyze garbage collection candidates and remove safe unreachable content, expired commits, redundant variants, and pruned activity records.
--dry-run analyzes candidates without establishing a barrier or deleting objects.
--min-age <hours> sets the minimum orphan age threshold (0-8760, defaults to the profile retention minimum of 6h); protects concurrent sync uploads and makes scheduled automatic GC safe.
Safe to schedule automatically: checks for active writers or barriers read-only before mutation (returns remote_busy / BUSY when busy).
Subcommands: remove-writer, remove-barrier (use each subcommand with --help).
Example: kasumi gc Programming --dry-run
command_help.gc_remove-writer:
Usage: kasumi gc remove-writer <profile> <writer-id>

Remove one exact writer marker listed by remote writers.
Verify that its process is inactive and no Sync or maintenance is running.
No Sync or GC is performed.
Example: kasumi remote writers Programming
command_help.gc_remove-barrier:
Usage: kasumi gc remove-barrier <profile> [<barrier-id>] --confirm-abandoned

Remove an abandoned maintenance barrier after manual verification.
--confirm-abandoned is required; verify no GC or Sync is active on any device.
Omit <barrier-id> when only one barrier is active; specify <barrier-id> or its 32-hex token when multiple barriers exist.
Verifies physical identity and confirms absence; never runs Sync or GC.
Example: kasumi gc remove-barrier Programming --confirm-abandoned
command_help.repack:
Usage: kasumi repack <profile> [--dry-run] [--reclaim-dirty] [--bwlimit <rate>] [--concurrency <1..16>] [--full]

Consolidate fragmented Micro-Packs and loose small files from live local files.
Ensure the workspace is clean, stop Sync on other clients, and run fsck/gc separately as needed.
--dry-run previews consolidation without creating packs or mutating remote state.
--reclaim-dirty also reclaims large partially dead packs; old packs remain until 'kasumi gc'.
--full shows pack inventory breakdown and published commit details.
Example: kasumi repack Programming --dry-run
command_help.resolve-missing:
Usage: kasumi resolve-missing <profile> [--dry-run | --confirm]

Resolve unavailable content as logical deletions. Review pending paths first.
Lists eligible paths and asks confirmation before publishing; use --dry-run to preview
without deleting, or --confirm for non-interactive automation.
Example: kasumi resolve-missing Programming --dry-run
command_help.remote:
Usage: kasumi remote <subcommand> <profile> [arguments] [options]

Remote inspection. Supports [--bwlimit <rate>] [--concurrency <1..16>]. Subcommands:
  heads, tree, commits, summary, stat, log, commit, get, restore, epochs, epoch,
  contents, content, markers, objects, orphans, writers, health
Use kasumi remote <subcommand> --help for required arguments and restrictions.
Example: kasumi remote summary Programming
command_help.config:
Usage: kasumi config

Interactive profile wizard: create, clone, edit, set key, change key storage, rename and delete profiles.
No profile operand. Changes are saved by each wizard action.
Example: kasumi config
command_help.remote_heads:
Usage: kasumi remote heads <profile>

List current logical heads.
command_help.remote_tree:
Usage: kasumi remote tree <profile> [--head <selector>]

Show a remote tree. --head must select a current logical head; required when multiple heads exist.
Example: kasumi remote tree Programming --head <commit>
command_help.remote_commits:
Usage: kasumi remote commits <profile>

List reachable commits.
command_help.remote_summary:
Usage: kasumi remote summary <profile> [--full]

Show a general vault summary and recent shared operational activity.
--full shows machine IDs and the complete recorded activity list.
command_help.remote_stat:
Usage: kasumi remote stat <profile> <path> [--commit <id>]

Show properties of a logical path in the effective tree or a reachable commit.
Use --commit <64-hex> to inspect a historical snapshot retained on the remote.
Quote paths containing spaces; pass -- before option-looking paths.
command_help.remote_commit:
Usage: kasumi remote commit <profile> <id>

Show commit details. <id> must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
command_help.remote_get:
Usage: kasumi remote get <profile> <path> <destination> [--commit <id>]

Download and authenticate one logical file from the effective tree or a reachable commit.
Use --commit <64-hex> to restore an older file version retained on the remote.
Destination must not already exist. Quote paths containing spaces. Does not modify the local profile.
command_help.remote_epochs:
Usage: kasumi remote epochs <profile>

Show the epoch chain.
command_help.remote_epoch:
Usage: kasumi remote epoch <profile> <selector>

Show epoch details. Selector is an epoch identifier or sequence number.
command_help.remote_contents:
Usage: kasumi remote contents <profile> [--audit]

List content metadata. --audit downloads and cryptographically validates physical contents.
Example: kasumi remote contents Programming --audit
command_help.remote_content:
Usage: kasumi remote content <profile> <id>

Show content details. <id> must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
command_help.remote_markers:
Usage: kasumi remote markers <profile>

Classify physical head markers.
command_help.remote_objects:
Usage: kasumi remote objects <profile>

Inspect the physical namespace.
command_help.remote_orphans:
Usage: kasumi remote orphans <profile>

List orphans; does not run GC or remove objects.
command_help.remote_writers:
Usage: kasumi remote writers <profile>

List writers and the maintenance barrier.
command_help.remote_health:
Usage: kasumi remote health <profile>

Full remote health diagnostic. Findings still return 0; inspection failure returns 1.
Does not replace the fsck payload audit.
command_help.options:
Global option: --lang <code>, before the command (en or pt-BR).
Automation options: --quiet (suppress progress and success output), --json (structured JSON on list/show/diagnostics/key/daemon/ignore/status/sync/fsck/gc/repack/resolve-missing/conflicts/profile/remote summary|writers|stat|get|log|restore), --log-file <path> (append clean UTF-8 text logs or NDJSON lines with --json).
Transport options: --bwlimit <rate> and --concurrency <1..16> override profile transport settings on network commands.
Help: -h, --help. Duplicate, unknown or valueless options are rejected.
command_help.list:
Usage: kasumi list

List configured profile names, one per line.
command_help.show:
Usage: kasumi show <profile> [--full]

Show local profile settings, last sync result, accepted commit authorship, and offline cached activity without contacting remote storage.
--full shows complete commit IDs, machine IDs, and recorded local and cached histories.
command_help.diagnostics:
Usage: kasumi diagnostics [<profile>] [--json] [--quiet]

Inspect local environment, rclone availability/version, disk space, and profile health (including .kasumiignore syntax) without accessing remote storage or exposing secrets.
Example: kasumi diagnostics --json
command_help.key:
Usage: kasumi key <profile> [--replace] [--json] [--quiet] [--log-file <path>]

Re-enter or replace the stored cryptographic key (password and salt, or KASUMI_MASTER_KEY / KASUMI_PASSWORD + KASUMI_PASSWORD2) for a profile.
Does not re-encrypt remote data; replacing a different existing key requires --replace (or interactive confirmation).
Use after switching key_storage in kasumi config or config.toml.
Example: kasumi key Programming --replace
command_help.profile:
Usage: kasumi profile <subcommand> <profile> [options]

Non-interactive profile management. Subcommands:
  create, edit, clone, storage, rename, delete, test
Use kasumi profile <subcommand> --help for arguments and options.
Supports --json, --quiet, and --log-file <path>.
command_help.profile_create:
Usage: kasumi profile create <name> --local <dir> --remote <dst> [--key-storage vault|file|memory] [--min-depth <1..4096>] [--min-age <1..8760>] [--bwlimit <rate>] [--concurrency <1..16>] [--rclone-config <path>] [--watch on|off] [--sync-interval <0|10..86400>] [--gc-interval <0..8760>] [--paused on|off] [--verify]

Create a profile non-interactively. Uses KASUMI_MASTER_KEY or KASUMI_PASSWORD + KASUMI_PASSWORD2 (or prompts on terminal).
--verify tests connectivity and vault authentication after saving, rolling back the profile on failure.
command_help.profile_edit:
Usage: kasumi profile edit <name> [--local <dir>] [--remote <dst>] [--min-depth <1..4096>] [--min-age <1..8760>] [--bwlimit <rate> | --clear-bwlimit] [--concurrency <1..16> | --clear-concurrency] [--rclone-config <path> | --clear-rclone-config] [--watch on|off | --clear-watch] [--sync-interval <0|10..86400> | --clear-sync-interval] [--gc-interval <0..8760> | --clear-gc-interval] [--paused on|off] [--allow-empty-local]

Update an existing profile's paths, retention, daemon schedule, or transport settings without moving files or remote data.
--allow-empty-local permits relocating a populated profile to a missing or empty local folder.
command_help.daemon:
Usage: kasumi daemon <subcommand> [arguments] [options]

Continuous multi-profile sync daemon with warm rclone sessions, native directory watching, zero-walk fast polling, and RAM-pinned key storage.
Subcommands:
  run [--foreground | --background]   Run daemon in foreground or detach in background.
  stop                                Stop the running daemon gracefully.
  status [<profile>] [--full]         Show daemon status, live stage/progress, and per-profile state.
  sync [<profile>] [--wait]           Trigger an immediate sync cycle.
  pause <profile>                     Pause automated sync/GC for a profile.
  resume <profile>                    Resume automated sync/GC for a profile.
  unlock <profile>                    Load a memory-mode profile key into daemon pinned RAM.
  lock <profile>                      Wipe a profile key from daemon pinned RAM.
  reload                              Reload config.toml profile definitions.
  logs [<profile>] [-f] [--lines <n>] Read or follow events from daemon.log.
  autostart <install|uninstall|status> Manage user-session autostart registration.
Supports --json, --quiet, and --log-file <path>.
command_help.profile_clone:
Usage: kasumi profile clone <source> <new-name>

Clone a profile configuration and master key with fresh empty local state.
command_help.profile_storage:
Usage: kasumi profile storage <name> <vault|file|memory>

Change a profile's local key storage mode. Switching from vault/file deletes the previously persisted key.
command_help.profile_rename:
Usage: kasumi profile rename <old-name> <new-name>

Rename a profile and migrate its private state and OS vault entry.
command_help.profile_delete:
Usage: kasumi profile delete <name> --confirm

Delete local profile configuration, persisted key, and SQLite state (--confirm is required).
Preserves synchronized local files and remote objects.
command_help.profile_test:
Usage: kasumi profile test <name> [--json] [--quiet] [--log-file <path>]

Validate profile credentials and test connectivity and authentication against remote storage without modifying local or remote state.
command_help.ignore:
Usage: kasumi ignore <subcommand> <profile> [arguments] [options]

Inspect or initialize '.kasumiignore' rules for a profile. Subcommands:
  check, init
Use kasumi ignore <subcommand> --help for arguments and options.
Supports --json, --quiet, and --log-file <path>.
command_help.ignore_check:
Usage: kasumi ignore check <profile> [--] <path...> [--json] [--quiet] [--log-file <path>]

Evaluate how one or more paths are classified by the profile's '.kasumiignore' and Kasumi's reserved internal exclusions.
Reports managed, ignored_protected, or ignored_disposable along with the winning rule and line number.
Example: kasumi ignore check work build/app.exe src/main.cpp
command_help.ignore_init:
Usage: kasumi ignore init <profile> [--preset default|dev|office|minimal] [--force] [--dry-run] [--json] [--quiet] [--log-file <path>]

Create a recommended '.kasumiignore' template in the profile's local root.
Use --force to overwrite an existing '.kasumiignore', or --dry-run to preview the template without writing.
Example: kasumi ignore init work --preset dev --dry-run
command_help.conflicts:
Usage: kasumi conflicts <profile> [--json] [--quiet]
       kasumi conflicts resolve <profile> <path> (--keep-canonical | --keep <artifact>) [--dry-run]

Scan the profile's synchronized folder read-only (respecting .kasumiignore) for '.kasumiconflict_*' artifacts, or resolve a preserved conflict group.
Example: kasumi conflicts work --json
command_help.completion:
Usage: kasumi completion <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>

Print shell completion script to stdout.
Example: source <(kasumi completion bash)
command_help.conflicts_resolve:
Usage: kasumi conflicts resolve <profile> <path> (--keep-canonical | --keep <artifact>) [--dry-run] [--json] [--quiet] [--log-file <path>]

Resolve one preserved conflict group by keeping either the canonical file or one '.kasumiconflict_*' artifact (matched by full path, filename, or origin suffix such as 'local' or 'remote').
The selected artifact is atomically promoted over the canonical path before any artifact is removed.
Example: kasumi conflicts resolve work docs/report.txt --keep local
command_help.remote_log:
Usage: kasumi remote log <profile> <path> [--full] [--json] [--quiet] [--log-file <path>]

List reachable commits that added, modified, deleted, or observed <path> without stopping at the cached frontier.
Example: kasumi remote log Programming docs/report.txt
command_help.remote_restore:
Usage: kasumi remote restore <profile> [<prefix>] <dst> [--commit <id>] [--dry-run] [--json] [--quiet] [--log-file <path>]

Download and cryptographically verify all files under <prefix> (or root '/' when omitted) into an empty directory <dst> that does not overlap the profile local folder.
Example: kasumi remote restore Programming docs /tmp/restored-docs --commit <64-hex>
